Saliency-weighted edge entropy with spatial controls

Source: R/saliency_features.R
compute_saliency_features.Rd

Filters an image once and weights the resulting edges by mean-normalized saliency. Returns image structure, map concentration, and control diagnostics separately. The existing compute_edge_entropy() result layout is unchanged.

Usage

compute_saliency_features(
  image,
  saliency,
  representation,
  signed_policy = "reject",
  image_id = if (is.character(image)) image else "image",
  max_pixels = 120000L,
  gabor_bins = 24L,
  filter_length = 31L,
  maxdiag = 500L,
  circ_bins = 48L,
  ranges = list(c(20L, 80L), c(80L, 160L), c(160L, 240L)),
  pairwise = TRUE,
  pair_weighting = "both",
  edge_selection = "image",
  validity = "legacy",
  min_cell_mass_fraction = NULL,
  min_effective_pairs = NULL,
  centre_sigma = 0.25,
  transform_controls = TRUE,
  donor_maps = list(),
  donor_assignments = NULL,
  scales = NULL,
  scale_units = "relative",
  pixels_per_degree = NULL,
  provenance = list(),
  use_cpp = TRUE,
  centre_match = FALSE,
  donor_aspect_tolerance = 0.01,
  min_common_coverage = 0,
  boundary = c("zero", "reflect")
)

Arguments

image

Grayscale numeric matrix or image file path. Matrix axes follow compute_edge_entropy()/imager conventions; the map must have the same axes.

saliency

Nonempty numeric matrix of aligned saliency values.

representation

Required: "weights" or "log_density" (natural logs).

signed_policy

For raw weights: "reject", "rectify", or "shift".

image_id

Target identifier used in donor assignments; defaults to the path for file inputs and "image" for matrices.

max_pixels

Analysis pixel count for file inputs, as in compute_edge_entropy(). NULL disables resizing; matrices are not resized.

gabor_bins, filter_length, maxdiag, circ_bins, ranges

Filter and pairwise settings as in compute_edge_entropy(). Ranges are inclusive distance-index bounds, not a new physical-distance convention.

pairwise

Calculate pairwise features and support diagnostics.

pair_weighting

"both" for saliency at both endpoints or "reference".

edge_selection

"image" holds the selected edges fixed across controls; "saliency" also changes selection and is a separately labelled sensitivity.

validity

"legacy" uses the native legacy mass cutoff (approximately mass > 1) in both backends. "support" uses explicit support thresholds. Both backends use Euclidean distance geometry.

min_cell_mass_fraction, min_effective_pairs

Required nonnegative support thresholds when validity is "support". Cell fraction uses all counted mass.

centre_sigma

Gaussian centre-bias standard deviation as a fraction of each image dimension (one or two values). This is an explicit descriptive control, not a fitted human fixation model.

transform_controls

Include exact flips and grid-preserving rotations.

donor_maps

Named list of maps, with the same representation and declared model/preprocessing as the target.

donor_assignments

Output of saliency_donor_assignments(). NULL reports donor controls as unavailable; no random pixel map is substituted.

scales

Optional multiscale block sizes. NULL skips multiscale output.

scale_units, pixels_per_degree

Units and conversion for multiscale output; see saliency_multiscale_entropy().

provenance

List recording model/version, smoothing, and other source details supplied by the caller. No additional smoothing is applied here.

use_cpp

Use compiled filtering, batched counting and statistics.

boundary

Convolution boundary handling, as in compute_edge_entropy(): "zero" (default, historical) or "reflect", which avoids artificial frame edges. Whole-image and foreground-weighted features differ in how much weight frame responses receive, so use "reflect" when comparing them.

centre_match

Also include a centred Gaussian fitted to the observed map's effective_fraction. This matches location entropy, not shape or pair support. Unattainable fits on the discrete grid are explicitly unavailable.

donor_aspect_tolerance

Maximum relative aspect-ratio error for donor maps (default 0.01). Resizing and before/after location metrics are recorded.

min_common_coverage

Minimum fraction of distance-direction cells shared by all maps in a comparison, within each range. Below this fraction, common contrasts are NA. Zero requires at least one shared cell; it is not a scientifically validated support threshold.

Value

A list with features (one row per map/control), ranges (pairwise range summaries), cells (per-control support tables), multiscale, selection (selected coordinates per control), comparisons (separate transform and donor family summaries), and metadata. Differences named observed_minus_control use each map's own valid cells. Pairwise differences named observed_minus_control_common use their intersection, with the same equal-directions-then-equal-distances reduction for both maps. Family comparisons intersect cells across the observed map and all usable, distinct nonidentity maps in that family, and report the mean, SD and range of control entropies, coverage, retained mass, controls used, and status. n_requested counts candidate rows (including unavailable placeholders), n_available counts rows with available descriptors, and n_controls counts distinct nonidentity maps. Repeated donor maps receive one vote. On observed rows, observed_minus_transform_mean and observed_minus_donor_mean copy the corresponding family contrast; other rows have NA. Pairwise family contrasts always use common support. Entropies are in bits. Zero mass is NA with an explicit status.

Details

Pair effective count measures weight concentration, not independent samples. Weighting changes the image descriptor; concentration need not decrease entropy. Unweighted differences describe the overall effect of weighting, while transforms and donors help assess alignment. Donors preserve their own concentration, not necessarily the target's. Matching effective_fraction alone does not match effective pair support. Low coverage or effective support calls for inspecting cells, even when a range value is available. Uniform saliency preserves native legacy outputs. The historical geometry and validity differences remain only in compute_edge_entropy(use_cpp=FALSE); the new API agrees across backends within floating-point tolerance. Controls sharing an edge set are counted in one geometry pass with one unweighted baseline. Saliency-based selection can require separate passes. Donor and transformed-map comparisons are descriptive, not permutation tests.

Examples

img <- outer(seq_len(12), seq_len(12), function(x, y) sin(x) + cos(y))
sal <- matrix(1, 12, 12)
result <- compute_saliency_features(img, sal, "weights", pairwise = FALSE,
  filter_length = 5L, gabor_bins = 4L, transform_controls = FALSE)
result$features[, c("control", "first_order", "effective_fraction")]
#>             control first_order effective_fraction
#> 1          observed    1.946194          1.0000000
#> 2        unweighted    1.946194          1.0000000
#> 3       centre_bias    1.989252          0.7782512
#> 4 donor_unavailable          NA                 NA
